summary: Strong medieval ensemble with broadly distinct everyday roles, an unmistakable king and a readable travelling jester. The main weaknesses are rigid slab-like garments, several modern-looking costume shapes, and insufficiently prominent distant-court identity.
problems: Breadmaker, elder and king share hip-fixed, two-tier skirt boxes spanning both legs. Visible horizontal ledges make the garments look assembled rather than draped, and the lower sections cannot follow individual leg movement.
The carpenter reads partly as a modern work shirt and shorts beneath an apron. The contrasting cylindrical hat crown reinforces a boater-like appearance rather than a rough straw work hat.
Broad rectangular shoulder pieces read as rigid plates, particularly on the elder. The messenger's upright cone reads more like a miniature wizard hat than a soft medieval hood.
The messenger's diagonal strap sits forward of the torso rather than against it; the breadmaker's apron similarly stands away from the upper skirt.
The jester clearly communicates performer and traveller, but the small split-diamond badges do not establish a distant court at stream scale.
fix: Carpenter: Lengthen the belted tunic into a clearly split thigh-length garment, with each lower section following its own leg; replace the exposed shorts-like colour blocks with continuous hose. Make the hat crown and brim one straw palette, using a shallow tapered crown and slightly irregular brim. Keep the projecting mallet. Breadmaker: Replace the stepped skirt slabs with overlapping, progressively flared panels; attach lower panels to the respective legs while preserving a closed gown silhouette at rest. Fit the whole apron against the gown instead of suspending it forward. Reduce the rectangular shoulder tabs into a close-fitting cloth neckline; retain the pale coif and loaf. Market Elder: Give the robe a distinct straighter silhouette with overlapping leg-following lower panels, not the breadmaker's identical stepped skirt. Break the broad shoulder bar into sloped mantle sections that clear the arms. Enlarge the chaperon's folded roll and show a substantial connected cloth tail; retain the beard, clasp and staff. Young Messenger: Replace the upright cone with a backward-drooping hood point continuous with the hood and liripipe. Seat the diagonal strap directly on the chest and connect it visibly to the satchel. Keep the short hem, tall boots and contrasting scroll. King: Preserve the crown, royal palette, ermine and sceptre. Replace the stepped lower robe with a continuous-looking arrangement of overlapping leg-following panels. Taper the mantle from fitted shoulders and pull its long side strips behind the arms so they remain clear during movement. Far-Court Jester: Preserve the three-point cap, counterchanged motley and travelling pack. Enlarge the split-diamond livery into a bold shoulder/back panel and repeat it prominently on the outward-facing bedroll or pack. Keep those shapes visible from the 40-degree camera without competing with the king's crown. Check every kit in idle, walking and arm-swing poses on both bodies.
